item.title: [New] Exchange Online sending from aliases is generally available: users can send and reply from any proxy address once the tenant switch is on
item.description:
Once enabled, outbound mail can carry any proxy address of a mailbox, including onmicrosoft.com addresses, so detections and transport rules keyed to the primary SMTP address miss mail a compromised account sends from an alias.

Exchange Online · Check whether SendFromAliasEnabled is on, set onmicrosoft.com domains to SendingFromDomainDisabled, and review transport and journaling rules and sender-based detections for alias addresses.

item.title: [New] Reject Direct Send is generally available: one org setting rejects unauthenticated mail that spoofs your own domains; new tenants get it on by default
item.description:
Direct Send is the path phishing kits use to deliver mail that looks internal and skips SPF alignment checks on the From header; this setting closes it for your own domains.

Exchange Online · Read the Change Optics Report, create partner inbound connectors for scanners and apps that send as your domain, then run Set-OrganizationConfig -RejectDirectSend $true and watch NDRs with 5.7.68 for a week.
